faq.q: Who is eligible to file ITR-1 (Sahaj)?
faq.a: ITR-1 (Sahaj) is for resident individuals with a total income up to ₹50 lakhs, whose income sources include salary/pension, income from one house property, and income from other sources (like interest and family pension). Agricultural income up to ₹5,000 is also permitted.

faq.q: Can ITR-1 be filed if I have income from two house properties?
faq.a: No, if you have income from more than one house property, you are not eligible to file ITR-1. You would need to file ITR-2 instead, which accommodates income from multiple house properties.

faq.q: What if I have capital gains income? Can I use ITR-1?
faq.a: No, any income from capital gains, whether short-term or long-term, disqualifies you from filing ITR-1. Individuals with capital gains must file either ITR-2 or ITR-3, depending on their other income sources.

faq.q: Is it mandatory to file ITR-1 online?
faq.a: While you have the option to file ITR-1 offline (by generating an XML file and uploading it), the online mode through the Income Tax e-filing portal is generally recommended for its ease of use and pre-filled data features.

faq.q: What documents do I need to file ITR-1?
faq.a: You will need your PAN, Aadhaar, Form 16, bank statements for interest income, investment proofs for deductions (e.g., 80C, 80D), and details of any other income. It's also advisable to check Form 26AS, AIS, and TIS.

faq.q: What is the income limit for filing ITR-1?
faq.a: The total income limit for filing ITR-1 (Sahaj) is ₹50 lakhs for the Assessment Year 2026-27. If your total income exceeds this threshold, you will need to file a different ITR form, typically ITR-2.
